description: Numbers that limits.single-source.guard finds bound to a limit-worded name and that are legitimately not members of the single limits policy (02-system-architecture.md invariant 6 and 'The single limits policy'; ARCH-16). One entry per declaration, matched on file and name so a moved line does not rot the register, with a reason that says why the value is not a product cap. The guard fails on an entry that matches nothing, so a number that goes away takes its exemption with it. Adding an entry is a review decision, never a way past a red guard: a cap the client pre-validates, the tests drive to its boundary, or GET /meta.limits publishes belongs in packages/contracts/src/limits.ts.

allowed.name: PORT_MAX
allowed.reason: 65 535 is the top of the TCP port range, and this is the upper bound EnvSchema validates PORT against. It is the width of the field, not a ceiling Iridium chooses, so there is nothing for a client to pre-validate or for GET /meta.limits to publish.

allowed.name: ZSTD_LEVEL_MAX
allowed.reason: 19 is the top of zstd's own compression-level range, and this is the bound EnvSchema validates BACKUP_ZSTD_LEVEL against. Like PORT_MAX it describes an external tool's input domain rather than a limit the product enforces on its own data.

allowed.name: PRESSURE_MAX_EVENT_LOOP_DELAY_MS
allowed.reason: The default for an environment key, and rule 2 of the single limits policy keeps environment names out of LIMITS: EnvSchema owns every default inline, where the key is declared. The load-shedding threshold is a per-deployment operational knob (11-operations-and-deployment.md, 'Metrics'), published to no client and driven by no client-side pre-flight.

allowed.name: PAT_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS
allowed.reason: The default for an environment key, per rule 2 of the single limits policy, beside PAT_DEFAULT_LIFETIME_DAYS and PAT_ALLOW_NO_EXPIRY. Token lifetime policy is chosen per deployment and enforced server-side at issuance; it is not one of the caps a client validates a request against before sending it.

allowed.name: PAT_ROTATION_OVERLAP_MAX_HOURS
allowed.reason: The default for an environment key, per rule 2 of the single limits policy. The rotation overlap window is deployment policy for how long a superseded token keeps working, enforced only server-side, and no client reads or pre-validates it.

allowed.name: HEALTHZ_MAX_EVENT_LOOP_LAG_MS
allowed.reason: A liveness-probe threshold, declared beside READINESS_RECHECK_MS and NOT_READY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS, which ARCH-02 fixes in the same place. It decides what /healthz says about this process rather than what the server accepts, so it is neither a request cap nor a content cap and no client sees it.

allowed.name: CLIENT_VERSION_MAX_LENGTH
allowed.reason: The length an inbound X-Iridium-Client-Version header is truncated to before it is recorded. It bounds what the server writes to its own logs from an untrusted header, refusing nothing and rejecting no request, so there is no boundary for a test to drive or for a client to respect.

allowed.name: HSTS_MAX_AGE_SECONDS
allowed.reason: The Strict-Transport-Security max-age helmet emits: one year, as the security-headers table fixes it. It is the value of an HTTP response header, read by browsers and not by Iridium, and changing it changes a header rather than what any request or document may contain.

allowed.name: maxRssBytes
allowed.reason: Zero is @fastify/under-pressure's 'disabled' sentinel, not a byte budget: the plugin sheds on event-loop delay and heap usage, both of which come from config.ops, and the RSS check is deliberately off. Recording a limit for it would invent a cap that is not enforced.

allowed.name: USER_AGENT_MAX_BYTES
allowed.reason: 255 is the width of sessions.user_agent VARCHAR(255) (03-data-model.md section 3) and the byte cut 04-auth-and-access-control.md section 11.1 applies to audit_events.context.user_agent. It bounds what the server records from an untrusted header, refuses no request, and is published to no client, so it is a column width rather than a product cap.

allowed.name: CLIENT_VERSION_MAX_CHARS
allowed.reason: 32 is the width of sessions.client_version VARCHAR(32) (03-data-model.md section 3). The header parser already caps X-Iridium-Client-Version at CLIENT_VERSION_MAX_LENGTH before it is read; this second cut only fits the recorded value to its column, refuses nothing and is seen by no client.

allowed.name: maxAge
allowed.reason: Zero is the Max-Age that expires the __Host-iridium_session cookie on logout (04-auth-and-access-control.md section 4.3: Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0). It is the value of a Set-Cookie attribute the browser reads, exactly like the HSTS max-age, and not a budget the server enforces on anything.

allowed.name: max
allowed.reason: The property model samples a dimensionless position in [0, 1] before scaling it by the current document length. One is the endpoint of that mathematical interval, not a product limit or request budget.

allowed.name: flushMaxBytes
allowed.reason: Zero disables Hocuspocus batching in the unit-test document double. It is a library sentinel in test support, not a byte limit accepted or enforced by the production server.

allowed.name: HTTP_MAX_ERROR
allowed.reason: 599 is the last HTTP server-error status in the external HTTP status-code domain. The classifier preserves supported 4xx/5xx errors and maps out-of-domain values to 500; this is protocol validation, not an Iridium product budget.

allowed.name: MAX_PEERS
allowed.reason: Six is the generated convergence fixture peer count for the PR property model. The ten-peer nightly model has its own fixture size; neither value limits a production vault, document, or collaboration connection.

allowed.name: max
allowed.reason: The test model samples a dimensionless position in [0, 1] and a generated deletion of at most 12 UTF-16 units. These bounds shape generated test operations and do not constrain production edits.

allowed.name: maxLength
allowed.reason: Eight bounds one generated test insertion. The 1980 generated operations plus 20 mandatory restarts make the specified 2000-operation nightly fixture. These are test workload sizes, not product text or queue limits.

allowed.name: DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS_MAX
allowed.reason: 2 147 483 647 is the largest millisecond delay representable by Node timers. Above it Node clamps to 1 ms; EnvSchema and the driver adapter reject that invalid input domain. This is an external runtime representation bound, not a note, request or product budget.
